name: moneytree
title: Moneytree
description: View and manage your finances from Moneytree via Raycast
author: clins1994

preferences.name: autoReloginOnRefreshFailure
preferences.title: Auto Re-login
preferences.label: Automatically re-login when refresh token fails
preferences.description: When enabled, the extension will automatically attempt to re-login using your stored credentials if the refresh token expires or fails

commands.name: list-categories
commands.title: List Categories
commands.description: Lists Moneytree categories and creates or edits custom child categories

commands.name: list-budgets
commands.title: List Budgets
commands.description: View monthly category budget spending and manage saved limits

tools.name: get-credentials
tools.title: Get Credentials
tools.description: Get Moneytree credentials and linked institutions, including connection status, account counts, refresh metadata, errors, and total balances.

tools.name: get-accounts
tools.title: Get Accounts
tools.description: Get Moneytree accounts with balances, currencies, types, statuses, and linked credential or institution names.

tools.name: search-transactions
tools.title: Search Transactions
tools.description: Search Moneytree transactions by date range, account, category, or description and return signed amounts with account context.

tools.name: get-categories
tools.title: Get Categories
tools.description: Get Moneytree transaction categories with ids, parent relationships, category types, and custom category flags.

tools.name: get-budgets
tools.title: Get Budgets
tools.description: List synced Moneytree category budget limits with category names. Read-only; does not calculate spent or remaining amounts.

tools.name: create-budget
tools.title: Create Budget
tools.description: Create a synced Moneytree budget limit for an expense category without an existing limit. Mutates real financial data; use only when the user explicitly asks to save this category and amount.

tools.name: update-budget
tools.title: Update Budget
tools.description: Change the saved limit of an existing Moneytree expense category budget. Mutates real financial data; use only when the user explicitly asks to edit, change, or update the existing limit to a specified amount. A request to create a budget is not permission to update an existing one.

tools.name: delete-budget
tools.title: Delete Budget
tools.description: Remove an existing Moneytree category budget limit. Mutates real financial data; use only when the user explicitly asks to delete that specific budget.

tools.name: update-transaction
tools.title: Update Transaction
tools.description: Update a Moneytree transaction's custom description and category. This mutates Moneytree data and should only be used when the user explicitly asks to edit a specific transaction.

tools.name: create-category
tools.title: Create Category
tools.description: Create a custom Moneytree subcategory under an existing parent category. This mutates Moneytree data and should only be used when the user explicitly asks to create a category.

tools.name: update-category
tools.title: Update Category
tools.description: Update a custom Moneytree category's name, parent, or icon. This mutates Moneytree data and should only be used when the user explicitly asks to edit a custom category.

ai.instructions: Moneytree stores financial credentials/institutions, accounts, categories, and transactions. Use get-credentials for institution connection status and grouped balances, get-accounts for account balances and account metadata, get-categories for transaction category ids, get-budgets for saved category budget limits (not spending progress), and search-transactions for spending, income, merchant, date, and account-specific questions. When a name could be a category, budget, account, or merchant, check categories and budgets first (and accounts if relevant); if exactly one match remains, proceed with it; if more than one remains (for example both a category and an account share the name), do not pick one or combine them as filters, and ask the user which one they mean before searching transactions. For spending in a category or budget, resolve the category id with get-categories or get-budgets and pass it as categoryId to search-transactions; never search a category or budget name as query text, because query only matches merchant descriptions. Treat transaction amounts as signed values: negative amounts are spending and positive amounts are income or refunds. To update a transaction, first use search-transactions to identify the exact transaction and get its original date, amount, claimId, and expenseType, then use get-categories to find the target category id, then call update-transaction only when the user explicitly asks to edit that specific transaction. To create a category, use get-categories to find the required top-level parent category id, then call create-category only when the user explicitly asks to create a subcategory. To edit a custom category, use get-categories to identify the existing custom category id, then call update-category with the requested name, top-level parent, or icon changes only when the user explicitly asks to edit that category. For budgets, resolve the exact expense category with get-categories and inspect existing limits with get-budgets before writes; do not guess category IDs. Suggestions, plans, or requests to compare budgets are read-only, not permission to save them. Call create-budget only for an absent category. If asked to create a budget but one already exists, do not reinterpret the request as permission to update it; explain the existing limit and ask whether to replace it with the requested amount. Call update-budget only when the user explicitly asks to change, edit, or replace an existing budget limit with a specified amount. Call delete-budget only for an explicitly identified saved limit, after the user accepts the concrete change. Do not expose secrets or ask for Moneytree passwords in chat. If a question requires more rows than returned, call search-transactions with a larger maxPages or a narrower date range.
